cards.front: Where is the murmur of mitral regurgitation heard, and what are its common causes?
cards.back: A **holosystolic**, high-pitched, blowing murmur at the **apex** that radiates to the **left axilla**. Causes: **mitral valve prolapse**, **ischemic papillary muscle dysfunction or rupture** (after MI), LV dilation, **rheumatic** disease and **infective endocarditis**.
cards.back_pt: Sopro **holossistólico**, agudo, regurgitativo, em jato de vapor, no **ápice**, com irradiação para a **axila esquerda**. Causas: **prolapso da valva mitral**, **disfunção ou ruptura isquêmica do músculo papilar** (pós-IAM), dilatação do VE, doença **reumática** e **endocardite infecciosa**.

cards.front: What are the auscultation findings and the valve pathology in mitral valve prolapse?
cards.back: A **mid-systolic click** (sudden tensing of the chordae) followed by a **late systolic murmur** at the apex. The leaflets show **myxomatous degeneration**. It is associated with **Marfan** and **Ehlers-Danlos** syndromes and can progress to mitral regurgitation.
cards.back_pt: Um **clique mesossistólico** (tensionamento súbito das cordas tendíneas) seguido de **sopro telessistólico** no ápice. Os folhetos mostram **degeneração mixomatosa**. Associa-se às síndromes de **Marfan** e de **Ehlers-Danlos** e pode evoluir para insuficiência mitral.

cards.front: What murmur and pulse findings suggest chronic aortic regurgitation?
cards.back: A high-pitched **early diastolic decrescendo** murmur at the left sternal border, heard best with the patient leaning forward. A large stroke volume plus diastolic backflow gives a **wide pulse pressure**, **bounding (water-hammer) pulses** and **head bobbing**.
cards.back_pt: Sopro **protodiastólico em decrescendo**, aspirativo, agudo, na borda esternal esquerda, mais audível com o paciente inclinado para a frente. O grande volume sistólico somado ao refluxo diastólico gera **pressão de pulso alargada** (PA divergente), **pulsos amplos, em martelo d'água** e **sinal de Musset** (oscilação da cabeça).

cards.front: What are the exam findings of mitral stenosis, and what does left atrial enlargement cause?
cards.back: **Loud S1**, an **opening snap** after S2, then a low-pitched **mid-diastolic rumble** at the apex. Pressure backs up and the **left atrium** dilates, causing **atrial fibrillation**, **mural thrombus** with stroke risk, and sometimes **dysphagia** or **hoarseness** from compression.
cards.back_pt: **B1 hiperfonética**, **estalido de abertura** após a B2 e, em seguida, **ruflar mesodiastólico** grave no ápice. A pressão se transmite para trás e o **átrio esquerdo** dilata, causando **FA**, **trombo mural** com risco de AVC e, às vezes, **disfagia** ou **rouquidão** por compressão.

cards.front: How do inspiration, Valsalva or standing, and squatting or handgrip change murmurs?
cards.back: **Inspiration**: more venous return to the right heart, so **right-sided murmurs** get louder. **Valsalva/standing** (less preload): **HCM** louder, **MVP** click earlier. **Squatting** (more preload and afterload) or **handgrip** (more afterload): **MR, AR and VSD** louder; HCM softer; MVP click later.
cards.back_pt: **Inspiração**: mais retorno venoso ao coração direito, então os **sopros de câmaras direitas** aumentam. **Valsalva/ortostatismo** (menos pré-carga): sopro da **CMH** aumenta, clique do **PVM** mais precoce. **Agachamento** (mais pré e pós-carga) ou **handgrip** (mais pós-carga): **IM, IAo e CIV** aumentam; CMH diminui; clique do PVM mais tardio.

cards.front: What are the characteristic histologic lesions of acute rheumatic carditis?
cards.back: **Aschoff bodies**: **granulomas** with **fibrinoid necrosis**, lymphocytes, plasma cells and **Anitschkow cells** (activated macrophages with a wavy, "caterpillar" chromatin bar). The inflammation is a **pancarditis**, and the **mitral valve** is the valve most often involved.
cards.back_pt: **Corpúsculos de Aschoff**: **granulomas** com **necrose fibrinoide**, linfócitos, plasmócitos e **células de Anitschkow** (macrófagos ativados com cromatina em barra ondulada, "em lagarta"). A inflamação é uma **pancardite**, e a **valva mitral** é a mais acometida.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension has 2 months of increasing leg swelling. Blood pressure is 112/70 mm Hg and pulse is 88/min. The jugular veins are distended with large v waves, and the liver pulses with each heartbeat. There is a holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border. The murmur becomes louder when she breathes in deeply. Which lesion is the most likely cause of this murmur?
choices: Ventricular septal defect
Mitral regurgitation
Aortic stenosis
Tricuspid regurgitation
Mitral valve prolapse
questions.explanation: Pulmonary hypertension dilates the right ventricle and causes **tricuspid regurgitation**. **Inspiration** increases venous return to the right heart, so right-sided murmurs get louder (**Carvallo sign**). Large v waves and a pulsatile liver show blood flowing back into the right atrium and veins. A VSD also gives a holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border, but it does not get louder with inspiration and does not explain the venous findings.
questions.explanation_pt: A hipertensão pulmonar dilata o ventrículo direito e causa **insuficiência tricúspide**. A **inspiração** aumenta o retorno venoso ao coração direito, então os sopros de câmaras direitas aumentam (sinal de Rivero-Carvallo). Ondas v amplas e fígado pulsátil mostram o refluxo de sangue para o átrio direito e as veias. A CIV também produz sopro holossistólico na borda esternal esquerda baixa, mas não aumenta com a inspiração e não explica os achados venosos.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man with Marfan syndrome comes for a routine visit. He is tall with long arms and fingers, and he had a dislocated lens as a teenager. He reports occasional palpitations. Blood pressure is 124/72 mm Hg. At the apex there is a mid-systolic click followed by a short late systolic murmur. When he stands up from a squat, the click moves earlier, closer to S1. Which finding would most likely be seen on histology of the affected valve?
choices: Myxomatous degeneration with accumulation of proteoglycans in the leaflets
Commissural fusion with dense fibrosis and new blood vessels
Dystrophic calcification of the valve cusps
Friable vegetations of platelets, fibrin and bacteria
Granulomas with fibrinoid necrosis and Anitschkow cells
questions.explanation: A mid-systolic click that moves earlier on standing, followed by a late systolic murmur, is **mitral valve prolapse**. Its valve shows **myxomatous degeneration**: proteoglycan-rich, floppy, redundant leaflets, often linked to connective tissue disorders such as **Marfan syndrome**. Commissural fusion and fibrosis are the chronic changes of rheumatic heart disease, which typically causes mitral stenosis, not a click.
questions.explanation_pt: Um clique mesossistólico que se antecipa ao ficar em pé, seguido de sopro telessistólico, indica **prolapso da valva mitral**. A valva mostra **degeneração mixomatosa**: folhetos redundantes e frouxos, ricos em proteoglicanos, muitas vezes ligados a doenças do tecido conjuntivo como a **síndrome de Marfan**. Fusão comissural e fibrose são alterações crônicas da cardiopatia reumática, que costuma causar estenose mitral, e não um clique.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old man has 6 months of fatigue and an uncomfortable pounding heartbeat when he lies on his left side. Blood pressure is 164/48 mm Hg and pulse is 84/min. His peripheral pulses are bounding, and his head nods slightly with each heartbeat. A high-pitched, decrescendo murmur starts right after S2. It is heard best along the **right** upper sternal border with the patient sitting up and leaning forward. Echocardiography shows a dilated aortic root. Which valve lesion is most likely?
choices: Mitral stenosis
Aortic stenosis
Aortic regurgitation
Pulmonic regurgitation
Mitral regurgitation
questions.explanation: An **early diastolic decrescendo** murmur with a **wide pulse pressure** and **bounding pulses** is **aortic regurgitation**; here the cause is **aortic root dilation**. Blood leaks back into the left ventricle in diastole, so diastolic pressure falls, while the larger stroke volume raises systolic pressure. Pulmonic regurgitation also causes an early diastolic decrescendo murmur, but it does not widen the systemic pulse pressure. Murmurs from aortic root dilation are often loudest at the right sternal border.
questions.explanation_pt: Sopro **protodiastólico em decrescendo** com **pressão de pulso alargada** e **pulsos amplos** indica **insuficiência aórtica**; aqui a causa é a **dilatação da raiz da aorta**. O sangue reflui para o ventrículo esquerdo na diástole, então a pressão diastólica cai, enquanto o maior volume sistólico eleva a pressão sistólica. A insuficiência pulmonar também causa sopro protodiastólico em decrescendo, mas não alarga a pressão de pulso sistêmica. Sopros por dilatação da raiz da aorta costumam ser mais audíveis na borda esternal direita.

questions.stem: A 10-year-old boy has 5 days of fever and painful, swollen joints. The pain moved from his knees to his ankles and then to his elbows. Three weeks ago he had a sore throat that was not treated. Temperature is 38.4°C (101.1°F). There is a new holosystolic murmur at the apex that radiates to the axilla, and pink rings with pale centers are seen on his trunk. Antistreptolysin O titer is high, and a throat culture is now negative. Which mechanism best explains the damage to his heart?
choices: Direct bacterial invasion of the valve leaflets
Immune complex deposition with complement activation
Superantigen activation of T cells by a streptococcal exotoxin
An exotoxin that blocks protein synthesis in myocytes
Antibodies against streptococcal M protein that cross-react with cardiac proteins
questions.explanation: This is **acute rheumatic fever** after group A streptococcal pharyngitis, with carditis (mitral regurgitation), **migratory polyarthritis** and **erythema marginatum**. Antibodies against the bacterial **M protein** cross-react with heart proteins (**molecular mimicry**), a **type II hypersensitivity** reaction. Immune complex deposition (type III) is the mechanism of poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis, not rheumatic carditis. The negative culture fits an immune process rather than infection of the valve.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **febre reumática aguda** após faringite por estreptococo do grupo A, com cardite (insuficiência mitral), **poliartrite migratória** e **eritema marginado**. Anticorpos contra a **proteína M** bacteriana reagem de forma cruzada com proteínas cardíacas (**mimetismo molecular**), uma reação de **hipersensibilidade tipo II**. A deposição de imunocomplexos (tipo III) é o mecanismo da glomerulonefrite pós-estreptocócica, e não da cardite reumática. A cultura negativa é compatível com um processo imune, e não com infecção da valva.

notes.title: Valvular disease: murmurs, maneuvers and rheumatic fever
notes.body_md:
## Systolic murmurs

- **Mitral regurgitation**: **holosystolic** murmur at the apex, radiating to the **axilla**. Causes include MVP, ischemic papillary muscle dysfunction, LV dilation, rheumatic disease and endocarditis.
- **Mitral valve prolapse**: **mid-systolic click** plus a late systolic murmur. **Myxomatous degeneration**; linked to **Marfan** and **Ehlers-Danlos** syndromes.
- **Tricuspid regurgitation**: holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border that gets louder with **inspiration**.

## Diastolic murmurs

- **Aortic regurgitation**: **early diastolic decrescendo** murmur at the left sternal border. **Wide pulse pressure** and **bounding pulses**.
- AR causes: **bicuspid aortic valve**, **aortic root dilation** (Marfan, syphilitic aortitis), **endocarditis** and rheumatic disease.
- **Mitral stenosis**: **opening snap**, then a **mid-diastolic rumble** at the apex. A shorter S2-to-snap interval means more severe stenosis.
- MS enlarges the **left atrium**: atrial fibrillation, thrombus and stroke.

## Bicuspid aortic valve

- The **most common** congenital heart valve anomaly.
- Also linked to dilation of the ascending aorta.
- It calcifies earlier than a normal valve, so aortic stenosis appears at a younger age. It can also cause AR.
- Associated with **coarctation of the aorta** and **Turner syndrome**.

## Maneuvers

- **Inspiration**: right-sided murmurs louder.
- **Valsalva** or **standing** (less preload): most murmurs softer; **HCM** louder; MVP click earlier.
- **Squatting** (more preload and afterload) or **handgrip** (more afterload): MR, AR and VSD louder; HCM softer; MVP click later.

## Acute rheumatic fever

- Follows **group A streptococcal pharyngitis** by about 2 to 4 weeks.
- **Molecular mimicry**: antibodies against **M protein** attack heart tissue (type II hypersensitivity).
- **Jones criteria** combine evidence of recent strep infection with major findings: **carditis**, **migratory polyarthritis**, **subcutaneous nodules**, **erythema marginatum** and **Sydenham chorea**.
- Histology: **Aschoff bodies** with **Anitschkow cells**.
- **Mitral valve** is most often affected, then the aortic valve. Repeated attacks lead to chronic valve fibrosis.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Sopros sistólicos

- **Insuficiência mitral**: sopro **holossistólico** no ápice, com irradiação para a **axila**. Causas: PVM, disfunção isquêmica do músculo papilar, dilatação do VE, doença reumática e endocardite.
- **Prolapso da valva mitral**: **clique mesossistólico** seguido de sopro telessistólico. **Degeneração mixomatosa**; associado às síndromes de **Marfan** e de **Ehlers-Danlos**.
- **Insuficiência tricúspide**: sopro holossistólico na borda esternal esquerda baixa que aumenta com a **inspiração**.

## Sopros diastólicos

- **Insuficiência aórtica**: sopro **protodiastólico em decrescendo** na borda esternal esquerda. **Pressão de pulso alargada** e **pulsos amplos**.
- Causas de IAo: **valva aórtica bicúspide**, **dilatação da raiz da aorta** (Marfan, aortite sifilítica), **endocardite** e doença reumática.
- **Estenose mitral**: **estalido de abertura** seguido de **ruflar mesodiastólico** no ápice. Um intervalo B2-estalido mais curto indica estenose mais grave.
- A EM aumenta o **átrio esquerdo**: FA, trombo e AVC.

## Valva aórtica bicúspide

- A anomalia valvar congênita **mais comum**.
- Também se associa à dilatação da aorta ascendente.
- Calcifica mais cedo que uma valva normal, então a estenose aórtica surge em idade mais jovem. Também pode causar IAo.
- Associada à **coarctação da aorta** e à **síndrome de Turner**.

## Manobras

- **Inspiração**: sopros de câmaras direitas aumentam.
- **Valsalva** ou **ortostatismo** (menos pré-carga): a maioria dos sopros diminui; o da **CMH** aumenta; o clique do PVM fica mais precoce.
- **Agachamento** (mais pré-carga e pós-carga) ou **handgrip** (mais pós-carga): IM, IAo e CIV aumentam; CMH diminui; clique do PVM mais tardio.

## Febre reumática aguda

- Ocorre cerca de 2 a 4 semanas após **faringite por estreptococo do grupo A**.
- **Mimetismo molecular**: anticorpos contra a **proteína M** atacam o tecido cardíaco (hipersensibilidade tipo II).
- Os **critérios de Jones** combinam evidência de infecção estreptocócica recente com achados maiores: **cardite**, **poliartrite migratória**, **nódulos subcutâneos**, **eritema marginado** e **coreia de Sydenham**.
- Histologia: **corpúsculos de Aschoff** com **células de Anitschkow**.
- A **valva mitral** é a mais acometida, seguida da aórtica. Surtos repetidos levam à fibrose valvar crônica.
